(men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] | years15 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team15 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years16 = 2022 | team16 = [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] | years17 = 2022 | team17 = [[Manama Club (basketball)|Manama Club]] | years18 = 2023 | team18 = [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] | years19 = 2024 | team19 = [[Gladiadores de Anzoátegui]] | highlights = * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Sporting News|SN]] ([[2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2010]]) * First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2010) }} '''Jordan Lee Crawford''' (born October 23, 1988){{cite web|url=http://www.goxavier.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/crawford_jordan00.html |title=Player Bio: Jordan Crawford – XAVIER OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE |publisher=GoXavier.com |access-date=June 4, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100829220204/http://www.goxavier.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/crawford_jordan00.html |archive-date=August 29, 2010 }} is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] and the [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier Musketeers]].{{cite news|title=Spreading the Word About Xavier's Jordan Crawford|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/21/sports/ncaabasketball/21crawford.html|access-date=June 4, 2010|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 20, 2010}} His brother is [[Joe Crawford (basketball, born 1986)|Joe Crawford]], who has also played in the [[NBA]]. ==Early life== Crawford was born to parents Joseph Sr. and Sylvia Crawford{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/columns/story?columnist=forde_pat&id=3146892 |title=Younger Crawford, Indiana get best of Kentucky – Columnist – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=December 8, 2010 |access-date=June 4, 2010}} in [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]] in 1988. In high school, he had suffered an [[ankle]] injury which forced him to miss his senior year of basketball. He attended Detroit's Communication and Media Arts High School and the prep school, [[Hargrave Military Academy]], in [[Chatham, Virginia]]. ==College career== ===Indiana University=== Crawford [https://web.archive.org/web/20101210125846/http://iuhoosiers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111606aaa.html signed] a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play at [[Indiana University]] and enrolled in 2007. Crawford played 30 games as a [[2007–08 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|freshman]] at [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] starting eight times and finished seventh among [[Big Ten Conference]] freshmen in scoring with 9.7 points per game, while helping Indiana finish 25–8 overall, 14–4 in the Big Ten and advancing to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]]. Crawford scored in double figures 15 times as a freshman, including a career high 21 points in Indiana's win at [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] on February 23, 2008, and had a near perfect night from the floor at Northwestern going for 6-for-7 overall and 4-for-5 behind the three-point line while handing out all five of his assists. He also made all five of his free throw attempts at the free throw line. Indiana recorded a 13–2 record when Crawford scored in double figures. ===Xavier University=== After fallout from the [[Kelvin Sampson#NCAA violations|Kelvin Sampson controversy]], Crawford transferred to [[Xavier University]] in 2008. [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] was one of only two nonconference regular season losses for the Hoosiers in the 2007–2008 season when Crawford was at [[Indiana University]]. Having been denied immediate eligibility by the [[NCAA]], Crawford had to sit out the 2008–2009 season, but was able to still practice with the [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Musketeers]]. In the summer of 2009, rumors abounded that a college player dunked on [[LeBron James]] in a pickup game at a mini-camp cosponsored by James and [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]]. Adding to the tale, amateur videos of the game and subsequent [[Slam dunk|dunk]] were allegedly [https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4315071 confiscated] by Nike at the behest of James. Later, Nike claimed there was a standing policy of no taping at the camp. It was then reported that it was in fact Jordan Crawford, a sophomore guard at Xavier, that made the feat at the LeBron James Skills Academy. Footage leaked out about a week later on [[YouTube]].{{cite web|last=Lopresti |first=Mike |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/columnist/lopresti/2010-03-19-xavier_N.htm |title=Xavier making new highlights with Jordan Crawford and Chris Mack |publisher=Usatoday.Com |date=March 19, 2010 |access-date=June 4, 2010}}{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/paul_daugherty/02/10/crawford/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100213195615/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/paul_daugherty/02/10/crawford/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 13, 2010 |title=Jordan Crawford, the kid who dunked on LeBron, a star at Xavier - Paul Daugherty - SI.com |publisher=Sportsillustrated.cnn.com |date=February 10, 2010 |access-date=June 4, 2010}} Crawford returned to play for the 2009–2010 season with the Muskies and led Xavier and the Atlantic 10 in scoring with 20.5 points per game, with .462 FG%. He scored in double figures in 31 straight games and 34 of XU's 35. Crawford scored 20+ in 20 games for the Musketeers and landed a spot on the First Team All-Atlantic 10. [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] won its 4th straight A-10 title and earned a 6-seed in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]]. Crawford led the Muskies past the 3-seed [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]] to its 3rd straight Sweet Sixteen, one of only two teams to accomplish during '08–'10. Xavier lost to the 2-seed [[2009–10 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State Wildcats]] in the West Regional semifinal in what [[CBSSports.com]] called "one of the best games in the history of the Sweet 16.".{{Cite news | title = Kansas State, Xavier put on a show for the ages | url = http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/13114975/kansas-state-xavier-put-on-show-for-the-ages | newspaper = CBSSports.com | date = March 26, 2010}} Crawford scored a career high 32 in the double overtime thriller including a deep three-pointer sending the game to the second overtime. Crawford earned a spot on the five-member NCAA Tournament All-West Region Team after averaging 29.0 points per game in the three appearances. Crawford scored more points (718) for a sophomore than any other in Xavier's history. He also finished 4th in the Musketeer's single season scoring history. Crawford was named by [[Sporting News]] a Third Team All-American and A-10 Player of the Year. Crawford entered the [[2010 NBA draft]] after two years of college play becoming the first Musketeer to enter the draft before graduating.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5064919 |title=Xavier guard Jordan Crawford exploring NBA draft options – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=April 9, 2010 |access-date=June 4, 2010}}{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/paul_daugherty/04/14/nba.exodus/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100422211537/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/paul_daugherty/04/14/nba.exodus/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 22, 2010 |title=Are Lance Stephenson, Jordan Crawford entering draft too early? - Paul Daugherty - SI.com |publisher=Sportsillustrated.cnn.com |date=April 14, 2010 |access-date=June 4, 2010}} At Xavier, Crawford wore the number 55. ==Professional career== [[File:Avery Bradley and Jordan Crawford.jpg|thumb|Avery Bradley and Jordan Crawford]] ===Atlanta Hawks (2010–2011)=== Crawford was selected by the [[New Jersey Nets]] with the 27th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. Due to his play style he was nicknamed "Sizzle". His rights were later traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] and he joined the team for the 2010 [[NBA Summer League]]. On July 9, 2010, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Hawks.{{cite news|title=Hawks Sign Rookie Jordan Crawford|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/205331/Hawks-Sign-Rookie-Jordan-Crawford|access-date=July 9, 2010|work=RealGM.com|date=July 9, 2010}} ===Washington Wizards (2011–2013)=== On February 23, 2011, Crawford was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] along with [[Maurice Evans (basketball)|Maurice Evans]] and [[Mike Bibby]] for [[Kirk Hinrich]] and [[Hilton Armstrong]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/trade_022311.html |title=Wizards Acquire Bibby, Evans, Crawford and First round Pick |work=NBA.com |date=February 23, 2011|access-date=February 23, 2011}} On March 8, 2011, Crawford scored a then-career high 22 points against the Milwaukee Bucks. On March 15, 2011, he passed his previous career high, scoring 27 points in a loss to the Chicago Bulls. He passed it again on March 30, 2011, by scoring 39 points in a loss to the Miami Heat. On April 1, 2011, Crawford recorded his first triple-double of his professional career in a game against the Cleveland Cavaliers. He had 21 points, 11 assists, and 10 rebounds. Crawford was the second Wizards rookie that season to record a triple double; [[John Wall]] had done so earlier that season.{{cite news|title=Jordan Crawford's triple-double powers Wizards past Cavs|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310401027|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213144729/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310401027|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 13, 2013|access-date=April 1, 2011|work=ESPN.com|date=April 1, 2011}} In the 2012–13 season, he was moved to point guard when John Wall missed time due to injury. He recorded his second triple-double with 27 points, 11 assists and 11 rebounds in a December game against the Atlanta Hawks. ===Boston Celtics (2013–2014)=== On February 21, 2013, Crawford was traded to the Boston Celtics for [[Leandro Barbosa]] and [[Jason Collins]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-acquire-jordan-crawford |title=Celtics Acquire Jordan Crawford |work=NBA.com |date=February 21, 2013 |access-date=February 22, 2013}} In his debut with the Celtics, he came off the bench to record 2 assists, 3 rebounds, and 10 points, shooting 4 for 9 from the field. Due to the injury of Rajon Rondo, Crawford became the starting point guard of the team at the beginning of the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]]. On November 29, 2013, he recorded his third triple-double with 11 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in a 103–86 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.{{cite news|title=Notebook: Celtics 103, Cavaliers 86|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131129/CLEBOS/gameinfo.html|access-date=November 29, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=November 29, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170415064221/http://www.nba.com/games/20131129/CLEBOS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 15, 2017|url-status=dead}} On December 9, 2013, Crawford was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week after averaging 23.3 points, 6.1 assists, and 3 rebounds on 61 percent shooting, helping the Celtics go 3–0 for the week.{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/wp/2013/12/09/former-wizards-guard-jordan-crawford-named-eastern-conference-player-of-the-week/ |title=Former Wizards guard Jordan Crawford named Eastern Conference player of the week |work=WashingtonPost.com |date=December 9, 2013 |access-date=December 10, 2013}} ===Golden State Warriors (2014)=== On January 15, 2014, a three-team trade was completed involving the Boston Celtics, the [[Golden State Warriors]], and the [[Miami Heat]]. The Celtics sent Crawford and [[MarShon Brooks]] to the Warriors. In exchange, the Celtics received [[Joel Anthony]], a protected future draft pick Philadelphia sent to Miami in an earlier trade, and a 2016 second-round draft pick from the Heat. The Heat also received [[Toney Douglas]] from the Warriors as part of the deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/crawford-brooks-trade-20140115|title=Warriors Acquire Jordan Crawford &
